newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurance.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurance.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it assigned its AA minus claims-paying ability rating to Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR), reflecting good management and strong capitalisation, plus sound reserving, investments, and operating performance.

"Offsetting these strengths, Standard & Poor's believes that the reinsurance sector as a whole faces considerable challenges, with growing competition in most lines and generally softening market terms," the agency said in a statement.
"Also, the gradual tendency in Continental Europe away from proportional to nonproportional reinsurance may reduce the stability of certain long-standing cedant relationships."
S&P said that SAFR's technical and overall operating performance should continue at around the 1995 level in the near term, despite some concerns about softening market rates.

"Although the company has a degree of exposure to catastrophic risks, very tight controls and extremely conservative reinsurance and reserving policies have significantly mitigated the potential net impact of claims," it said.
But it added that longer term, returns could suffer due to "increased competition through consolidation in SAFR's main markets of France and Germany, as well as internationally".
